ATF7-NPFF: Keep as a discovery CTA. The coding reference passes; tumor RNA does not establish the readthrough junction or the exact protein. Junction and protein identity are the priority.
CIMIP3: Keep as a discovery CTA. Mouse sperm structure supports its biological category. Tumor maxima are 1.2 TPM and 55.4 HPA pTPM in separate sources, so the lower TPM value alone does not justify low priority.
CTAGE15: Keep as a discovery CTA. Its cTAGE-family name is not antigen evidence. Verify this copy rather than borrowing other CTAGE results.
CTXND2: Keep as a discovery CTA. Placental association and the coding reference are the support; function and protein localization are uncharacterized.
DEFB113: Keep as a reproductive-secretory discovery candidate. HPA tumor RNA reaches 63.7 pTPM despite a 2.3 TPM maximum in the separate tumor source. Human tumor secretion has not been established.
ENSG00000237378: Keep as an embryo-associated discovery CTA. Establish a sequence-linked identity and endogenous protein detection before stronger claims.
ENSG00000241690: Keep as a testis-associated discovery CTA. Coding annotation and expression support inclusion; the broad scoring table supplies no independent functional validation.
ENSG00000258417: Keep as an embryo-associated discovery CTA. Resolve transcript and sequence identity before importing named-gene literature.
ENSG00000273155: Prioritize identity review. A shared mitochondrial ribosomal-protein annotation makes it essential to distinguish this locus from MRPL30-associated records before transferring normal or tumor protein evidence.
ENSG00000274944: Keep as a lower-confidence discovery CTA. The 110-aa canonical protein passes, with TSL 2 and no MANE designation. No exact-locus study was verified; database links to MYCBP are not evidence for this protein.
ENSG00000284934: Keep as an embryo-associated discovery CTA. Tumor RNA is substantial in at least one sample; exact-locus translation remains experimentally unverified.
ENSG00000289809: Lowest tumor-expression priority in this set: the recorded maximum is about 0.068 TPM. It passes the presence rule, but that is very weak evidence of a useful tumor target.
GOLGA8T: Keep as a discovery CTA, prioritizing copy-specific mapping in this duplicated family. Family homology does not establish this copy's protein production.
H2AL1Q: Keep as a germ-cell histone discovery candidate. The retrieved proteomics is mouse evidence; human copy-specific protein detection is missing.
LCN9: Keep as an epididymal-secretory discovery candidate. Mouse reproductive studies support the category; human tumor secretion is unverified.
MSANTD5: Keep as an early-embryo discovery CTA. Tumor maxima are 3.4 TPM and 12.2 HPA pTPM in separate sources. Its high developmental RNA establishes the association, while protein function remains uncharacterized.
OOSP4B: Keep as a maternal/oocyte discovery CTA. Its category comes from measured RNA; OOSP1 or OOSP4A experiments do not validate OOSP4B.
PABPN1L: One of the more biologically coherent discovery candidates: mouse experiments establish a maternal-to-zygotic transition role and human RNA supports the developmental association. Human protein and tumor evidence remain the next steps.
PRAMEF18: I recommend a normal-evidence review hold. A treated human vascular-cell study reports a combined PRAMEF18/PRAMEF19 feature; the responsible copy is unresolved. The current released label remains CTA.
PTTG1IP2: Keep as a lower-priority discovery CTA: little characterization and about 3.2 TPM maximum tumor RNA. PTTG1IP/PBF experiments do not establish this paralog's function.
SPADH: Keep as a reproductive discovery candidate. Human secretion and spermadhesin function need exact-sequence evidence; livestock spermadhesin studies do not establish them.
SSU72L2: Keep as an early-embryo discovery CTA. It has the highest recorded tumor TPM maximum in this gap set, but neither enzyme function nor endogenous protein follows from that RNA value.
SSU72L3: Keep as an early-embryo discovery CTA. Its RNA pattern is promising; resolve this copy independently of SSU72 and the other SSU72L loci.
SSU72L4: Keep as an early-embryo discovery CTA. Substantial tumor RNA warrants follow-up; family-wide phosphatase literature is not exact-copy protein evidence.
SSU72L5: Keep as an early-embryo discovery CTA. Substantial tumor RNA warrants follow-up; endogenous protein production and exact-copy attribution remain unverified.
TAF11L11: I recommend a normal-evidence review hold. The macrosatellite study reports family RNA in brain and testis without resolving this copy. The current released label remains CTA.
TAF11L13: I recommend a normal-evidence review hold. Family-level brain RNA cannot be assigned to, or dismissed for, this copy. The current released label remains CTA.
TAF11L14: I recommend a normal-evidence review hold. The same unresolved neural/reproductive macrosatellite signal applies; a separate copy-specific assay is needed. The current released label remains CTA.
TEDDM1: Keep as an epididymal discovery candidate. Reproductive RNA is strong; the retrieved discovery experiment is mouse evidence, not human tumor protein evidence.
UBTFL1: Keep as an early-embryo discovery CTA on independent human embryo RNA and its coding reference. The claimed human Ubtfl1 qPCR assay in Zhu 2021 uses primers matching mouse Sod1; do not credit that assay. UniProt has protein-level evidence, but this review did not resolve tissue-specific peptides.
